incidents.victim: Pope's Worldwide Prayer Network — Click to Pray app
incidents.vector: An insecure direct object reference (IDOR) in the Click to Pray API let anyone query sequential user IDs without authentication.
incidents.impact: More than 700,000 users' names, emails, and country data were exposed in plaintext, along with staff/admin account details; the flaw remained live as of publication.

incidents.vector: Attackers breached UpBound and stole customer information.
incidents.impact: Stolen data was used to fraudulently rent furniture and electronics via the Acima marketplace, generating roughly $13 million in fraudulent loan agreements.

incidents.vector: Not publicly disclosed; the company is notifying affected customers of a security breach.
incidents.impact: Exposed customer data included the last four digits of payment card numbers.

incidents.vector: Attackers used an autonomous AI agent (a version of the "Hermes" AI agent run in an unrestricted "YOLO mode") to breach the ministry's systems.
incidents.impact: The intrusion was discovered after a researcher found an internet-exposed directory containing the attacker's malware payloads and operation logs.

incidents.vector: Attackers obtained some of the cross-chain bridge's private keys and used them to sign fraudulent transactions.
incidents.impact: Approximately $24 million in cryptocurrency was stolen from the AFX Trade bridge.

incidents.victim: Zimbra Collaboration Suite users — governments and enterprises across NATO, Ukraine, CIS countries, and Africa
incidents.vector: A zero-click/half-click exploit of a Zimbra webmail zero-day (CVE-2025-66376) auto-runs malicious JavaScript the moment a phishing email is viewed, with no clicks required.
incidents.impact: Active since July 2025 and still hitting unpatched instances, the campaign exfiltrated 90 days of email, credentials, 2FA codes, and contact data from government, defense, transportation, financial, energy, and education-sector victims; CISA, NSA, FBI, and 15 allied nations issued a joint advisory.

incidents.vector: Not yet disclosed; a hacker sent the company samples of allegedly stolen records before Origin confirmed the breach.
incidents.impact: Customer account information, partial credit card and bank account numbers, names, addresses, and dates of birth were compromised for a subset of Origin's nearly 5 million customers.

incidents.victim: Johnson Controls C-CURE 9000 / victor (physical access control systems)
incidents.vector: Multiple flaws, including a critical SSRF/deserialization vulnerability (CVE-2026-21653, CVSS 9.6), allow unauthenticated remote code execution on the access-control application server and connected clients.
incidents.impact: Successful exploitation could let an attacker take control of physical security systems (badge readers, door controls) at critical infrastructure sites worldwide; CISA issued an ICS advisory urging immediate patching.

incidents.vector: Attackers compromised a third-party supplier's file-sharing platform using stolen credentials and stole technical documents.
incidents.impact: The Everest ransomware group demanded 10 million Swiss francs (~$12.3 million); Stadler refused to pay and filed a criminal complaint. Production and train operations were unaffected.

incidents.vector: A ransomware attack disrupted logistics and shipping systems, prompting Nichirei to sever internal networks.
incidents.impact: Shipments from Nichirei's roughly 7,000 refrigerated vehicles and 141 warehouses were curtailed, causing shortages for about 5,000 customers including KFC Japan franchises; personal data was stolen and partially leaked. RansomHouse claimed responsibility.

incidents.vector: A hacker gained access to the land registry's database and wiped it entirely after an extortion attempt failed.
incidents.impact: The nationwide property transaction system was paralyzed, preventing notaries from authenticating sales or registering mortgages across Romania.

incidents.victim: Office of the President of Kenya (website)
incidents.vector: Not disclosed; attackers compromised the presidential website.
incidents.impact: Hackers demanded a bitcoin ransom; Kenyan authorities are investigating the breach.

incidents.vector: Attackers chain two vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-60137 and CVE-2026-63030, to achieve remote takeover just three days after disclosure.
incidents.impact: Millions of WordPress sites are exposed to remote takeover, with exploitation attempts already widespread across one of the internet's largest attack surfaces.

incidents.vector: A newly disclosed deserialization flaw in SharePoint is being actively exploited in the wild.
incidents.impact: Researchers warn that patching alone is insufficient and organizations should rotate credentials on any assets that may have been exposed.

incidents.vector: A security threat affecting self-hosted ShareFile Storage Zone Controllers (not standard cloud-only accounts) prompted Progress to tell customers to shut the servers down.
incidents.impact: Organizations running on-premises Storage Zone Controllers face potential compromise of shared file infrastructure until remediated.

incidents.vector: Members of the Scattered Spider collective used social engineering and identity-based intrusion techniques to breach Transport for London's network in 2024.
incidents.impact: Two leading members, Thalha Jubair (20) and Owen Flowers (18), were sentenced in the UK to five and a half years in prison; a third alleged member, Peter Stokes, was extradited to the US to face charges tied to over 100 intrusions and $100 million-plus in ransom payments.

incidents.vector: Not disclosed; a cyberattack compromised systems across the clinic network.
incidents.impact: Patients who visited at least 21 Partnered Health clinics may have had medical records stolen.

incidents.victim: Critical infrastructure network devices (Communications, Defense, Energy, Financial Services, Government, Healthcare — global)
incidents.vector: FSB Center 16 actors scan for routers using default or weak SNMP community strings and exploit known Cisco Smart Install and web-portal vulnerabilities to exfiltrate device configurations.
incidents.impact: This decade-plus campaign has opportunistically compromised critical infrastructure networks worldwide; NSA, CISA, FBI, and agencies from a dozen-plus allied nations issued a joint advisory urging SNMPv3 adoption and network hardening.

incidents.vector: Not fully disclosed; the UK and EU member states formally attributed a December 2025 attack on Poland's energy grid to FSB Centre 16.
incidents.impact: Had it succeeded as intended, the attack could have caused roughly 500,000 civilians to lose electricity; the UK simultaneously sanctioned 24 individuals and entities tied to Russian cyber and hybrid operations.

incidents.victim: 1VPNS (First VPN Service) and associated ransomware infrastructure
incidents.vector: 1VPNS sold no-log VPN infrastructure to ransomware groups; a separate designee, Yevgeniy Silayev, sold "cryptor" tools that disguise malware from security software.
incidents.impact: OFAC sanctioned 1VPNS, its administrator Dmytro Rashevskyi, and Silayev; victims of ransomware attacks using 1VPNS infrastructure included U.S. businesses, financial firms, hospitals, and municipal governments. The action follows a May 2026 FBI-supported takedown of 1VPNS infrastructure.
